subject: SLA redlines: uptime targets, credit ladder, and scheduled maintenance windows
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@atlascloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Sullivan <tsullivan@atlascloud.com>, procurements@atlascloud.com
Date: Fri, 14 Feb 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Atlas - Order Form / SLA redlines

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Atlas is excited about Redwood's latency profile and multi‑region routing. As we prepare the purchase order, our procurement and SRE teams ran through the proposed MSA + Order Form and surfaced a few SLA redlines that need clarification before we can route to finance. I attached our markup (Atlas_SLA_Redlines_20250214.docx). High level asks: 

- Uptime target: we propose 99.99% monthly for core inference endpoints (production), or a clearer credit ladder if you hold to 99.95%.
- Service credits: Atlas prefers a linear credit ladder capped at 50% of monthly fees; credits should escalate by severity band and be applied to the affected billing region rather than global billing.
- Response times: P1 (production outage) 1 hour initial response / 4 hour remediation SLA; P2 4 hour initial / 24 hour remediation.
- Maintenance windows: request no more than one rolling maintenance per month per region during a 2‑hour local window; require 7 days advance notice and opt‑out for blackout weeks during product launches.

Can you confirm Redwood's position and provide a proposed redline that reconciles these items? If you can get legal eyes on the credit tapering language (we want it tied to affected region and measured per‑region uptime), that would speed approval on our side.

Thanks,
Emily Park
Sr. Procurement Manager
Atlas Cloud

Attachment: Atlas_SLA_Redlines_20250214.docx (docx, 34KB)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Emily Park <epark@atlascloud.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 15 Feb 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Atlas - Order Form / SLA redlines

Emily —

Appreciate the clear markup and the priorities. I looped in Aditya (sales leadership) and Lauren (contracts) so we can produce a single reconciled redline for Atlas. Quick responses to your bullets: 

- Uptime: Redwood's standard hosted offering is 99.95% monthly for single‑region endpoints; we can offer a 99.99% commitment on a committed‑capacity Order Form with a 12‑month minimum and an annual true‑up. Alternatively, we can implement a per‑region uptime measurement with a graduated credit ladder — see proposed table in the attached PDF.
- Credits: We generally cap credits at 50% of the monthly fee for a given billing period. We are open to per‑region crediting; we'll propose language that ties credits to the impacted region and to the specific model/route impacted rather than global account.
- Response times: We can meet 1 hour initial response for P1s and a 4 hour target for remediation with an agreed escalation path and optional 24/7 on‑call on Dedicated customers. P2 described is reasonable.
- Maintenance: We do rolling maintenance by default. Proposed compromise: one 4‑hour rolling maintenance window per region per quarter during 02:00–06:00 UTC with 72 hours notice; emergency maintenance excluded but will be communicated as soon as possible. We can add blackout exceptions for product launches per Atlas request.

Next steps: Lauren will draft the redline that (a) ties credits to a region & route, (b) makes the credit ladder asymmetric for partial degradations, and (c) documents the escalation ladder for incidents. We'll send a single PDF with tracked changes by EOD Monday. If acceptable, we can then route DocuSign for the Order Form.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Response_PROPOSED_20250215.pdf (pdf, 12KB)
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: Emily Park <epark@atlascloud.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Feb 2025 08:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Atlas - Order Form / SLA redlines

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding my draft redline. Key deviations call out so procurement can pre‑review: 

1) Measurement: we propose measuring uptime per region, per route (production inference route). Uptime calculation = (available_seconds / total_seconds) excluding scheduled maintenance windows and exclusions like customer network or third‑party outages.

2) Credit ladder (proposed):
- >=99.95%: 0% credit
- 99.90% to 99.95%: 10% of monthly fee for affected route/region
- 99.50% to 99.89%: 25%
- <99.50%: 50% (cap)

3) Response & remediation: P1 initial response within 1 hour; target time to mitigation based on severity (we won't promise full restoration time in the MSA but will document escalation handoffs and optional paid remediation SLAs on Dedicated).

4) Maintenance: allow quarterly rolling maintenance windows of up to 4 hours per region with 72h notice. We include an emergency maintenance clause (immediate action required to prevent data loss) with post‑incident credit evaluation (i.e., we don't treat emergency maintenance as a credit‑eligible outage unless caused by Redwood).

5) Region blackout / launches: add an Atlas‑requested blackout clause allowing Atlas to designate up to two calendar weeks per year as no‑maintenance windows for critical release events; these must be requested with 10 days notice.

I added tracked language around per‑region crediting and clarified that credits apply to the invoice line item associated with the affected route. Can you confirm Atlas' procurement/legal accepts the quarterly maintenance cadence and the credit ladder? If not, we can rework to monthly maintenance windows with a slightly tighter credit ladder.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks for the detailed draft. Procurement and SRE reviewed the ladder and the per‑region crediting approach looks good to us with a small ask: can we get the measurement definition tightened to include a 5‑minute sampling rule for token‑level failures and a post‑incident RCA window of 10 business days (otherwise credits are not eligible)? If you can include those two items in the tracked changes we can get this over to finance for signature.

Also please include a single DocuSign envelope that contains (a) MSA with redlines, (b) Order Form with committed capacity and the 99.99% option as an upsell line, and (c) the SOW if possible. Sending this to my team and procurement distribution now.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the DocuSign link.

Tom Sullivan
